questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer:
The university was highly ranked and a good reputation. I wanted to take law courses in spanish as Copenhagen University doesn't offer that. Likewise, it was free to choose and participate in sport courses.
The campus is extremely beautiful with a lot of outdoor areas connecting the different lines of study. There was a lot of outdoor cafe and food options and the university arranged many social activities for all of the students.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I had an absolutely amazing experience and I truly wish that I could come back for another semester.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Pretty easy. There was a one week orientation before classes started and we were also connected to a student organization called Hermanos sin fronteras who helped us with any social and travel related issues. We also had a contact person from the international office who we could contact any time concerning any issues related to visa or the university.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I arrived a week before orientation and had a hard time finding my way around and socializing.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I lived at City U which is a 2-5 minute walk from campus. I found it through the university's website so it was fairly easy.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: The university is located in a rather dangorous area of Bogotá. Be cautious about living in Canalaría and las Aguas even though it is cheap and close to the university. Chapinero - or the north of Bogota is really nice and safe, however you'll have to take a bus or an uber to the university.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I was confused to why we had to make a spanish essay after being accepted into the university.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Very confusing. They have two systems depending on wether the course you want to register has any requirements. If not, you get signed into the course as soon as you register. Otherwise, you'll be put on pending and can see the result after 1-2 weeks. There's no was to prioritize so you have to register subjects in the order you want them. Also, registration starts only 3 weeks before classes start which I found very stressful prior to registering. Some of my subjects was first accepted in the system a few days before class started.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: I could contact Anderson (the contact person from the international office). He created a Team group where we could talk with him and the other exchange students.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got the courses I wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: A danish saying: Hav is i maven.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I didn't feel challenged at all. The professors decide what reading material we had, how the exams should be and so on. Everything was up to the teacher. A lot of group work and very little individual assessment. The classes reminded me of the danish gymnasium, a lot of assignments, grades that didn't necessarily make sense, random quizzes during classes. In comparison to KU the exams were very informal and easy.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Too easy

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer:
In KU I have lectures and seminar classes. Attendance is voluntary and our grades are decided on one single exam on the end of the semester. 
In UniAndes we only had interactive seminar classes. A lot of presentations and in-class quizzes, mid-term exams and assignments, so the final exam was only 20-40% of my final grade.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Ética professional, derecho internacional II (ingles), contratos internacionales and criminología. 
Also salsa and bachata básico and Escalada en muro intermedio.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Contratos internacionales was a great and practical course. They take you through every step of a contract and give you recommendations throughout the course on how to improve, as well as take you through arbitration steps. 
I also really liked criminología. It's a smaller course and you get a good understanding of the different theories from a teacher that is really interested in the subject.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I travelled a lot more than I had expected which was very expensive

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: transportation was very cheap. Also eating out costed more or less the same as making food at home, so I ate out a lot.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I loved the bachata and salsa classes that the university offered. I think I danced 6+ hours a week. Hermanos sin fronteras also arranged some really nice social activities.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
A wide range of sport classes (dance, ball-games, martial arts, fitness etc.)
Many different student unions and clubs (book, pride, biodiversity, sport, cars, debate clubs etc.)

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Take part in the Hermanos sin Fronteras activities. They throw fun parties and arrange great trips around Colombia.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Travel as much as you can. Colombia is so beautiful! I would highly recommend these cities: Medellin, Cartagena, Villa de Leyva, Santa Marta, Barranquilla, Neiva (to see the Tatacoa Dessert), Leticia (to see the Amazon). In and around Bogotá I can recommend going to Gringo Tuesday (a language exchange that occurs every Tuesday of the year) and Andrés Carne de Res in Chia, which is the biggest one.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It took me a good 2 months to get accustomed. I had a lot of problems with culture shock, home sickness and language barriers in the beginning, but halfway through I get way better and had the time of my life.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Colombians are very open and warm people but you might have to initiate friendships. But as soon as you have made a friend they're very loyal and love to share their culture and traditions with you.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I looked very foreign (tall, pale, blonde, blue eyes) so I experienced a lot of staring and comments on my appearance. The meat tastes very strong and the food in general is very different. There was always latin music playing and people talk a lot especially gossip about other people.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The open and warmness that I was met with everywhere. People are extremely nice and curious about you. There was a more relaxed attitude towards time, we were more spontaneous and didn't necessarily meet on time. It was also great that everyone could dance without having to get drunk, the parties and socials were so much fun. Christmas traditions were also great, I can recommend going out with some local at la noche de las velitas.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Be social. It helps a lot on culture shock. 
Live in the moment. The exchange year passes by way too quickly. 
Say yes. Every day is an adventure in this country.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: No

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: I had a presentation in spanish for my final exam in criminology and I succeeded with really good grades.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The language barrier. My spanish is fairly good, however legal spanish was something else and if I zoned out in class I would be completely lost in translation.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: The only danger of going to Colombia is not wanting to leave. In all seriousness, fantastic country and amazing experience. Have a wonderful exchange!

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
